legacy.claim: No globally smooth steady single-valued flow branch exists around a moving core at any swept wind strength — the moving system's steady state, if any, is not a positive-x Bernoulli graph
legacy.evidence: ORB-10935's predeclared steady-existence measurable: caustic clip fractions at finest 0.740, 0.713, 0.573, 0.028 for U/v_GP ∈ {0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1}, ladder-stable across 41³/61³/81³. At low U partly structural (the near-radial GP inflow limit is not a positive-x graph), but the trans-critical wind also clips. ORB-10938 answered what the dynamics settle to: **a settled state exists at every (U, rung) by T = 600, and it is not the Bernoulli branch** — it violates the speed law beyond error and carries rung-stable vorticity, while its *direction* field lands near the marched branch's (multipole differences 0.02–0.18). So the marched construction found roughly the right wake geometry while imposing the wrong speed closure; the caustics were the graph ansatz's boundary, not the flow's
